lines: Welcome to the Wayfarer Guild, Avelorn chapter. The Sundering left machines running wild out there; we survey, we clear, we report.
Start in Dawnmeadow through the East Gate. Come back when the Mosskin herds are thinner.
Rations, tonics, all fresh. Prices are Guild-fixed, so don't haggle.
Sell me your field materials; I ship them to Sylvara.
Sit down, let me look at you. There, good as new.
The tonics I can't give you away, but the Merchant sells them.
The transit lattice still runs between camps. A little coin keeps the crystals charged.
Sylvara is further, and costs more.
Bring me materials and I'll make you something that keeps you alive.
Copper gears? Craglets swallow them. Don't ask me why.
East Gate. Dawnmeadow lies beyond: Mosskin and Sporelings. The amber mites are further east, on the Amber Trail.
If you see three dozen of anything chasing you, run back here.
North Gate to Whispergrass. Craglets and Thornbacks; not for a first day out.
The rune circle out there hums at night.
Mosskin graze north-west and won't bother you. Sporelings by the pond answer each other's cries.
Past the east road the Amber Trail is Ambermite country. They come to you.
The trail follows the old pipeline all the way to the windmill hills.
Gliders bolt when hurt; drive them against the trees.
Craglets nest in the scree, and they swallow gears. Bring me some back.
Thornbacks on the ridge travel in herds; take them together.
Rest a while. The Dustwings never stop coming while the sails turn.
I patch up more Wayfarers here than anywhere in Lumeris.
Sail Hill is all Dustwing. Pull forty and spin, if you're brave.
The millrace goes east to Moonbrook.
Brookfin won't bite unless you start it. The reeds in the marsh, though, spit.
Pull the Reedstalkers round a corner; they'll follow you into reach.
This was the finest orchard in Lumeris before the pump went wrong.
Mind the pump house. The rot grows thickest round it.
The rot comes from below. Something in Hollowroot is feeding it.
Clear the rows, then go down. You'll need the Guild Pass for the lift.
Guild Pass only beyond this point. Guild orders.
The Warden's in the Heart Chamber, east of the pump hall.
Going up? The lift reaches Avelorn or the orchard.
Mind your head on the roots.
Welcome to Sylvara, Wayfarer. The forest grows over everything here, machines included.
Start in Fernreach through the East Gate. The Graftlings there won't fight back; Mossbridge's newts and drones will.
Rations and tonics, carried up from Avelorn and marked up for the climb.
Bring me sap and scales; Duskhar's alchemists pay well for anything green.
Hold still. Spore rash, sap burns... nothing the lodge hasn't seen.
If you go down to the Basin, breathe through cloth.
The lattice runs between every camp in Verdantis, and to Avelorn and Duskhar beyond.
The further the jump, the more crystal it burns. Coin first.
Field drops make better supplies than the merchant's, if you bring enough of them.
Newt slick for vital tonic, moth scale for focus. Graftling twigs make decent bread ovens, too.
East Gate. Fernreach is ferns and Graftlings, nothing else.
The Graftlings won't touch you. Herd them up; it's good practice for Mossbridge.
North Gate to Mossbridge. Two old bridges over the creek; take either.
Newts croak for their whole bank, and the drones dive at anyone near their taps.
Graftlings everywhere here, and none of them fight. Gather a big herd before you swing.
The ruins up north are where the Aethrion grafted the first ones.
Hit one newt and the whole bank comes for you. Use that.
Hives are north of the creek, more drones on the north-west slope. Canopy Steps is up the north path.
Three terraces, two kinds of trouble. Hounds down here, moths in the middle, both on top.
Pull moths along the terrace; they can't shoot you through the walls.
The grafting engine stalled years ago. The Tenders went down to the Vineworks; the crawlers stayed.
The trellis rows funnel Vinecrawlers. Use that.
The press still turns, slowly. Something in it still wants grapes.
Tenders spray from range and patch each other up. Kill the ones at the back first.
Sit. Vine-lash and sap burns are most of my work.
The hares at the pump bolt the moment you touch them. Corner them first.
These are the oldest trees in Verdantis. The Aethrion ran their conduits through the roots.
Four Antlered Engines graze under the Eldest. Don't fight two at once.
The haze comes from the Engine's vents in the east. The bloats are born in it.
The Matrons that seed them live inside the Engine. Bring me bloat membranes and I'll prove it.
The Heartwood Engine's mouth. The Guild's been watching it since the spores thickened.
The Regent's in the heart chamber, past the piston hall. End it and the Basin will clear.
Root lift's working. Sylvara or the Basin?
Don't touch the sap lines; they bite.
Welcome to Duskhar, Wayfarer. Every mirror in Solenia still turns to follow the sun, and something is aiming them.
Start with the Saffron Dunes past the West Gate. The Sandcoils there won't trouble you unless you trouble them.
Water's free in Duskhar, thanks to the canal. Everything else costs.
Rations and tonics, brought up from Sylvara. Sell me your glass; the observatory buys it all.
Sunburn, glass cuts, heatstroke. Sit in the shade and drink this.
Out there, rest at the camps. The sand gives nothing back.
The lattice reaches every camp in Solenia, back to Sylvara, and on to Port Merrow.
Duskhar to the coast costs more. The crystals don't like salt air.
Sand and glass make good supplies if you know what to do with them.
Jackal pelts render down for vital tonic. Scarab glass makes a decent focus draught.
West Gate. The Saffron Dunes: Sandcoils on the crests and the glass, and jackals at the oasis.
Keep to the pipeline trail and you'll find the way north.
Caravan Gate. The road runs to Caravan Verge: brass kites overhead, glass scarabs in the washes.
Watch the sky there. The kites still survey the road, and the scarabs come for anyone.
Sandcoils bask on the crests and won't bite unless you start it.
Jackals at the oasis hunt as a pack. More Sandcoils sun themselves on the glass under the mesa.
The caravanserai is where three roads meet. Nobody's traded there in years.
Kites shoot from the heights. Pull them round the walls into reach.
Lightning fused this whole plain to glass. The Sentries still walk their old lines on it.
Basilisks call each other. Fight them one pack at a time.
The Dial still keeps Aethrion time. The Acolytes keep the Wardens running.
Kill the Acolytes first, or the Wardens just keep standing up.
Rest in the shade of the tent. The Dial's stone holds the heat all night.
The graveyard south of here is quieter if you need to catch your breath.
The canal's the last running water for leagues. The Striders live on it.
Herd them along the channel walls before they scatter. They skate the sluices and the cistern too.
The causeway runs to the Vault. The surveyors who sealed it never left.
Clear the Revenants and bring down two Colossi, and the Guild will trust you with the Key Prism.
Key Prism only. Guild orders, and the door's orders too.
The Sovereign sits under the heliostat, past the foundry. Shut it down.
The lift runs to Duskhar or the causeway.
Don't look straight into the mirrors.
Merrow chapter of the Wayfarer Guild. Out here the sea took the Aethrion machines, and the sea gives them back broken.
Start on Saltwind Shore through the East Gate. The Tidehoppers will show you how thick the packs run in Thalassia.
Rations, tonics, the same Guild prices as the mainland, plus the cost of shipping them here.
Bring me what the reef gives you. Merchants in Vaelspire pay well for anything from the sea.
Salt in a wound stings less than a Polyp barb. Hold still.
If you're heading for the reef, bring more tonics than you think you need.
The lattice runs between every camp on the islands. The tide doesn't bother it.
Duskhar and Vaelspire are further, and cost more. Crystal charge isn't cheap out here.
Kelp, hopper tendon, medusa jelly: all useful, once you know how to boil it.
I make rations and tonics from what you bring. Cheaper than the merchant, if you do the gathering.
East Gate. Saltwind Shore is past the dunes: hoppers at the tidepools, gulls on the cliffs.
The crabs on the wrack line bite back. Don't wander into them looking up at the gulls.
Ferry to Tidewheel Bay leaves from the end of the pier. Walk on, the pilot knows the way.
The bay's pumps still run, and so do the automatons that maintain them. Kelp tenders in the shallows, too.
Tidehoppers won't trouble you. The Gullwings will, once you're under the cliffs.
The reef path is past the east camp. Coral Reach starts where the sand turns pink.
Stay on the boardwalks where you can; the channel runs deep in the middle.
Spitters behind the coral heads will pick you apart. Draw them round to you.
Those wheels have turned for a thousand years and the automatons won't let anyone stop them.
Kill the kelp tenders first. They knit the others back together.
Off the ferry and straight into the kelp? Sit, let me look at you.
The bay air's good for you. The pumps' brine spray isn't.
Every hull out there is full of borers. Hit one and the whole wreck comes out.
The freighter's no better. The borers have eaten clean through to the cargo hold.
The skates run when you hurt them. Come at them from the open mud and they'll pile up against the pools.
That mast still pings something under the sea. The guardians around it don't like visitors.
Rays ride the storm round the masts. When the wind turns, so do they.
The turtles behind the breakwater move as a herd. Take them all or none.
The lightning out here isn't natural. It comes up from the relay.
Rest before you go to the hatch. There's no medic down there.
This hatch goes down to the Drowned Relay. The drones down there swarm the halls when the pumps surge.
Something below is still sending. If you can stop it, the machines up here might calm.
Going up? I can take you to the headland or all the way back to Merrow.
Mind the gallery. The jellies shield the drones.
Vaelspire chapter. The researchers here built half of what's trying to kill you out there, and they'd like it back in one piece.
Start at Frostline through the West Gate. The mites on the thaw strip are harmless; learn the cold on them.
Rations and tonics, Guild prices plus the cost of hauling them up the mountain.
Anything crystal sells well here. The labs buy everything.
Frostbite first, then the cuts. Hold your hands near the vent.
Stay out of the open snow at night. The cold does more than the monsters.
The lattice is clearer up here than anywhere. Cold crystals hold a charge.
Port Merrow and Cindervale cost more, but the crystals don't freeze.
Hare haunch, mite gel, wisp dust. The mountain feeds you if you know what to boil.
I'll make rations and tonics from your materials, cheaper than the merchant.
West Gate. Frostline's past the pines: mites, hares, and lights over the lake.
The lights shoot. Don't stand on open ice while they're watching.
The cable lift goes up to Snowcoil. Hold the rail, the wind is strong at the top.
The serpents up there came out of the coils, and the gear walkers still tend the dead pumps. Nobody knows how many serpents there are.
Hares run when they're hurt. Drive them north into the trees and they'll pile up.
Wisps over the lake hit from far off. Use the shore.
Rams on the terraces defend each other. Hit one, fight the flock.
Mind the chasm on the saddle. It's further down than it looks.
Welcome to the coils. The serpents fill those trenches faster than we can clear them.
The pump yard's gear walkers are slow. Don't let them corner you anyway.
Off the lift and into the cold. Let me warm those hands.
The steam vents are warm, but don't drink from them.
The plough mechs still run the road. Two of them, and they don't stop for anyone.
The vault doors at the east end are sealed. The keepers would like to keep it that way.
The reflections step out of the ice. Kill them first; they mend everything around them.
The big grazers on the south shore won't touch you unless you start it.
The ring conduit still carries power to the Archive. The sentries guard every pylon.
Specters are seeping out of the breach by the door. That's new.
This is the Archive door. Beyond it, the Curator keeps the records, and freezes anything that disturbs them.
If you mean to go in, go ready: the lancers inside shoot far. The lift keeper below can bring you back.
Going up? Back to the Circuit or all the way to Vaelspire.
The vault is past the index gallery. The lancers there shoot far.
Cindervale chapter of the Wayfarer Guild. Everything here was built to make iron, and most of it still thinks that's its job.
Start on the Ashfield flats past the East Bridge. Come back when the herds have thinned.
Rations and tonics, hauled up from Vaelspire. Heat spoils everything, so I charge what it costs to keep them cool.
Bring me Emberfall scrap; the foundries in the south buy all I can ship.
Burns, mostly. Hold still, the salve stings before it cools.
Drink water out there. More Wayfarers fall to the heat than to the imps.
The lattice runs hot here, but it runs. Every camp in Emberfall, or Vaelspire and Umbracrest for the long haul.
Umbracrest's beyond the Crucible. Nobody walks there twice.
Slag glands, vent bladders, cheap ash meat: I can turn your surplus into tonics for less than the shop asks.
Don't sell me Living Embers. Keep them. You'll know why soon enough.
East Bridge. Ashfield's beyond: grazers on the flats and the ridge, toads in the slag pools and round the old heat-sink.
If the bridge rattles, something big is crossing it. Step aside.
North Bridge, start of the old causeway. Forge country: hounds in the kennels, brass tenders in the cold forges, and the hounds still think they're on duty.
Hounds are faster than you. Don't run; stand and swing.
Ashcrawlers graze the flats and won't touch you. The toads in the slag pools will, and they bring their friends.
More toads squat by the heat-sink east of the crossroads. Hit one and the rest come.
The haul road crosses the lava stream once, on the iron bridge. Imps on both banks, and every one of them bites.
Imps fill the hollows west of the bridge, the scree under the falls and the old rail trestles.
The causeway runs over the Great Channel. Kennels to the east, cold forges to the west.
The brass spiders weld the hounds back together. Kill the spiders first.
Skinks ring the vent pool; pull them round it and they bunch up nicely.
The worms on the fissure spit from across the lava. Make them come to you.
Two spans left over the river: the High Span on the road, the Lower Span south.
Scraplings ring like bells when you hit one. Then all of them come.
The ring road goes round the lake. Don't take a short cut across it.
Wraiths in the channels east, Brutes on the scrap heap west and up in the mould yard.
Everything down there answers to something in the Zero Core. The foundry has a mind, and it's awake.
Clear the pour channels and the yard, then go down through the hatch.
Furnace Zero's below. The lift still works; the heat hits you at the bottom.
The core's at the far end, past the pens or through the stoker halls.
Going up? Cindervale or the Crucible rim.
Keep your hands off the rails; they're hotter than they look.
Umbracrest chapter, the last one on the road. Everything past these walls belongs to the Lattice now.
Start in the Dusk Verge, through the South Gate. Put out the wisps before they drink our last lamps.
Rations and tonics, brought in on the Cindervale transit. Nothing grows here any more, so nothing's cheap.
Bring me lattice scrap. The scholars upstairs pay in coin they don't need.
Shadow burns don't bleed; they go cold. Sit by the lamp while I work.
If you start seeing violet at the edge of your eyes, come straight back.
The lattice still carries us, for now. Every camp out there, or Cindervale if you need the heat.
Don't ask me who else is listening on the line.
Blooms, wisp cores, lurk bristles: I make tonics from what the city leaves us.
Lattice Nodes are the real treasure. Hold on to them.
South Gate. The Verge is all wisps and lurks; the wisps leave you be, but one squealing lurk brings the whole street.
If the lamps out there go dark, run toward the gate.
East Station. No trains have run since the Sundering, but the yards are busy all the same.
Mites in the sidings, drones on the gantries. Mind both.
Wisps drift on the boulevard and won't bother you. Lurks under the overpass will, all at once.
Mind the square under the obelisk: lurks there drag the wisps into the fight.
The flowers drink colour. Burn the beds first, or they shade everything fighting near them.
The glasshouses south are thick with blooms, and haulers circle the dead pond.
Coupler crews work the sidings; hit one and the whole yard comes.
Drones on the gantries can't shoot through the carriages. Use that.
Two ways across the tear: the bridge in the middle, the planks at the west end.
Riftlings come out of the edge faster than you'd like. Pull them away from it.
The Array still listens to the Lattice. Sentinels ring the great dish and walk the lines north of here.
The birds scatter when you hit them. Catch the whole flock in one swing.
Every lattice line in the city meets on that plaza. So do the glyphs.
Cut a Keysigil from the Executors in the court; the Warden won't open the Descent without one.
Whatever is in the Heart runs all of this. Every drone, every glyph.
Bring me the Keysigil, rest, and then go down. I'll be here when you come back up.
The Descent opens for the Keysigil and nothing else.
The Sovereign's chamber lies past the loom or through the spindle hall.
Back up? Umbracrest or the Gate.
Don't look at the lattice too long. It looks back.
